notes.front: What is Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management?
notes.back: A compliance solution that helps you detect, investigate and act on risky and malicious activity inside your organisation.
notes.explanation: It aims to minimise internal risks, the ones driven by employee activity rather than outside events.
notes.example: Like a bank’s internal fraud team watching for staff misuse, rather than the guards watching for robbers.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview?
notes.back: A feature that uses machine learning to find the most critical risks and apply protection controls automatically, according to each user’s risk.
notes.explanation: High-risk users get blocked from risky actions while low-risk users stay productive.
notes.example: Like a building pass that loses access to the server room when its holder behaves suspiciously, and gets it back when things settle.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Microsoft Purview Communication Compliance?
notes.back: An insider risk solution that detects, captures and acts on inappropriate messages that could lead to data security or compliance incidents.
notes.explanation: It checks text and image-based messages for business policy violations, for designated reviewers to examine.
notes.example: Like a newsroom editor reading drafts for libel before they go out, but for workplace chat and email.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Communication Compliance, “What is Communication Compliance?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is eDiscovery?
notes.back: Electronic discovery: identifying and delivering electronic information that can be used as evidence in legal cases.
notes.explanation: In Purview it lets you identify, review and manage content in Microsoft 365 services to support investigations.
notes.example: Like gathering the paper files a court asks for, but searching mailboxes, chats and sites instead of cabinets.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “Describe eDiscovery”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft Purview, what is an eDiscovery case?
notes.back: The container for all the searches, holds and review sets for one investigation.
notes.explanation: Creating a case is the step after a trigger event is escalated.
notes.example: Like a lawyer’s matter file that gathers every request, freeze order and evidence bundle for one dispute.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In eDiscovery, what is a hold?
notes.back: A way to preserve content that may be relevant to a case, securing it from deletion during the investigation.
notes.explanation: It guards against both accidental and intentional deletion.
notes.example: Like a “do not destroy” notice pinned to a filing cabinet while a dispute is under way.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In eDiscovery, what is a review set?
notes.back: A secure, Microsoft-provided Azure Storage location to which collected items are copied for review.
notes.explanation: It gives a fixed, known set of content that you can search, filter, tag and analyse.
notes.example: Like photocopying the relevant documents into a separate evidence room, so the originals stay where they were.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery features and capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Microsoft Purview Audit?
notes.back: Purview’s auditing solutions, which record user and admin operations across Microsoft 365 for searching later.
notes.explanation: It supports responses to security events, forensic and internal investigations, and compliance obligations.
notes.example: Like a building’s visitor log and camera footage, but for actions in Microsoft 365 services.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Describe audit in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is the unified audit log?
notes.back: The organisation’s single store of audit records for user and administrator activities across Microsoft 365 services.
notes.explanation: When an audited activity happens, a record is generated and stored there.
notes.example: Like one shared logbook for every door in a campus, instead of a separate book at each door.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “What the audit log captures”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Audit Standard?
notes.back: The base Purview auditing solution, on by default for organisations with the right subscription.
notes.explanation: It gives searchable audit events and a search tool without extra configuration.
notes.example: Like the basic recording plan that comes with a security camera: running from day one, but keeping only a set length of history.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Audit (Standard)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What is Audit Premium?
notes.back: The advanced Purview auditing solution, building on Audit Standard with longer retention, retention policies and intelligent insights.
notes.explanation: It also gives more bandwidth for pulling audit data, which helps large-scale investigations.
notes.example: Like upgrading a security camera plan to keep footage for a year and flag notable events.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Audit (Premium)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Audit Premium, what are intelligent insights?
notes.back: High-value audit records showing, for example, when mail items were accessed or forwarded and what a user searched for.
notes.explanation: They cover Exchange Online and SharePoint Online and help scope possible breaches.
notes.example: Like a library log that records which books someone opened, not just that they entered.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Audit (Premium)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which internal risks can Insider Risk Management help with? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: data leaks and spillage, confidentiality violations, intellectual property theft, fraud, insider trading, regulatory compliance violations.
notes.explanation: These are risks driven by internal events and employee activity, which can be avoided.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which kind of risk does Insider Risk Management target: that from external events, or from internal events and employee activity?
notes.back: Internal events and employee activity.
notes.explanation: External risks are outside an organisation’s direct control; internal ones can be eliminated and avoided.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Insider Risk Management principle balances user privacy against organisational risk through privacy by design?
notes.back: Transparency.
notes.explanation: The other principles are configurable, integrated and actionable.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Insider Risk Management principle means policies can be set by industry, geography and business group?
notes.back: Configurable.
notes.explanation: Policies can be tailored rather than one-size-fits-all.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Insider Risk Management principle refers to a workflow shared across Microsoft Purview solutions?
notes.back: Integrated.
notes.explanation: Cases can, for example, move on to eDiscovery for legal review.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Insider Risk Management principle is about insights that enable reviewer notifications and data and user investigations?
notes.back: Actionable.
notes.explanation: It is the fourth of the solution’s design principles.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What can insider risk analytics do before any insider risk policy exists?
notes.back: Evaluate potential insider risks, to show areas of higher user risk and which policies to consider.
notes.explanation: It needs no prior policy set-up.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Identifying potential risks with analytics”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In the Insider Risk Management workflow, what are policies built from?
notes.back: Predefined templates and policy conditions defining which risk indicators are examined.
notes.explanation: Conditions also set who is included, which services are prioritised and the monitoring period.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk management workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In the Insider Risk Management workflow, what generates alerts?
notes.back: Risk indicators that match policy conditions, automatically.
notes.explanation: Alerts appear in a dashboard showing those needing review and statistics over time.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk management workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: At the triage stage of Insider Risk Management, what can a reviewer do with an alert marked Needs review?
notes.back: Open a new case, add it to an existing case, or dismiss it.
notes.explanation: Reviewers can look at alert details, user activity, severity and profile information first.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk management workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which investigation tools does an Insider Risk Management case offer? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: user activity chart, content explorer, case notes, data risk graph.
notes.explanation: The case brings activity, policy conditions, alert and user details into one view.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk management workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which integration powers the data risk graph in Insider Risk Management investigations?
notes.back: Microsoft Sentinel.
notes.explanation: The graph maps links between users, devices, cloud resources and data flows in a case.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk management workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: At the action stage, how can Insider Risk Management reviewers resolve cases?
notes.back: By sending policy reminder notices to users, or escalating serious cases to eDiscovery (Premium) for legal investigation.
notes.explanation: Alert data can also be exported to external security tools.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk management workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What are the five stages of the Insider Risk Management workflow, in order?
notes.back: Policies, alerts, triage, investigate, action.
notes.explanation: Policies produce alerts, reviewers triage them into cases, investigate, then act.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk management workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which insider risk scenario covers staff downloading large volumes of files or emailing data to personal accounts before they leave?
notes.back: Data theft by departing users.
notes.explanation: Policy templates detect such activity whether the departure is voluntary or not.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk management workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which product’s signals help Insider Risk Management detect users disabling security features or installing unauthorised applications?
notes.back: Microsoft Defender for Endpoint.
notes.explanation: This is the security policy violations scenario.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk management workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Insider Risk Management, what are priority user groups for?
notes.back: Closer monitoring and more aggressive risk scoring of users in high-risk positions, such as executives.
notes.explanation: Administrators of information systems are another example of such users.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk management workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which activities can the Risky AI usage policy template detect? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: prompt injection attacks, accessing protected materials, sending sensitive data to AI services outside organisational controls.
notes.explanation: Its insights are also fed into Microsoft Defender XDR.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk management and AI interactions”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Through which Purview control does adaptive protection apply different sharing rules to users as their insider risk level changes?
notes.back: Data loss prevention (DLP) policies.
notes.explanation: The DLP policy applied to a user adjusts automatically as their level changes.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Through which Purview control does adaptive protection preserve content deleted by high-risk users?
notes.back: Microsoft Purview Data Lifecycle Management.
notes.explanation: A retention label policy preserves what the user deletes.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Through which Microsoft Entra control does adaptive protection restrict app access by insider risk level?
notes.back: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access.
notes.explanation: Conditional Access policies respond automatically to the user’s current risk level.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which solution calculates the insider risk levels that adaptive protection uses?
notes.back: Insider Risk Management, from each user’s behaviour and the risk indicators in the organisation’s policies.
notes.explanation: The levels sit at the centre of adaptive protection.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk levels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which insider risk level goes to users with high-severity alerts or several high-severity activity sequences, and gets the strongest controls?
notes.back: Elevated.
notes.explanation: It is the highest of the three levels.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk levels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which insider risk level goes to users with medium-severity alerts or several high-severity data exfiltration activities?
notes.back: Moderate.
notes.explanation: Its controls aim to balance security with productivity.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk levels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which insider risk level brings light controls, such as policy tips and educational reminders?
notes.back: Minor.
notes.explanation: It goes to users with low-severity alerts or at least one high-severity exfiltration activity.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk levels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When a user’s insider risk level falls, what happens to their adaptive protection controls?
notes.back: They relax automatically; when risk rises, they tighten, with no admin action.
notes.explanation: Levels update continuously from the user’s ongoing activity.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk levels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: With adaptive protection in DLP, do you need a separate static DLP policy for each risk scenario?
notes.back: No. The right DLP policy is assigned to the user automatically as their risk level changes.
notes.explanation: Adaptive protection assigns DLP policies dynamically.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Adaptive protection in Data Loss Prevention”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Under adaptive protection, for how long is content that an Elevated-risk user deletes from SharePoint, OneDrive or Exchange Online preserved?
notes.back: 120 days.
notes.explanation: A retention label policy does this automatically, so evidence stays available for investigation.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Adaptive protection in Data Lifecycle Management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In Microsoft’s example Conditional Access set-up, what might happen to an Elevated-risk user?
notes.back: They might be blocked from all organisational applications until their risk level is resolved.
notes.explanation: Lower levels might face a Terms of Use prompt or blocks on specific sensitive apps.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Adaptive protection in Conditional Access”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: By what means does adaptive protection help mitigate risk? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: context-aware detection, dynamic controls, automated mitigation.
notes.explanation: Automated mitigation also reduces admin overhead.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which apps’ messages can Communication Compliance evaluate? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: Teams, Viva Engage, Outlook, WhatsApp, among others.
notes.explanation: It covers both Microsoft and non-Microsoft apps.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Communication Compliance, “What is Communication Compliance?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What kinds of policy violation does Communication Compliance look for in messages? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: inappropriate sharing of sensitive information, threatening or harassing language, potential regulatory violations.
notes.explanation: Policies can be predefined or custom and check internal and external communications.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Communication Compliance, “What is Communication Compliance?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does Communication Compliance support separation of duties?
notes.back: With role-based access controls: one group sets up policies and permissions, and investigators and reviewers handle messages.
notes.explanation: This keeps configuration apart from message review.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Communication Compliance, “What is Communication Compliance?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In which Communication Compliance workflow stage do admins identify compliance requirements and set up policies?
notes.back: Configure.
notes.explanation: It is the first of four stages.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Communication Compliance, “What is Communication Compliance?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In which Communication Compliance workflow stage do admins use alerts, document reviews and user history to look into policy matches?
notes.back: Investigate.
notes.explanation: Issue management and filters also help at this stage.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Communication Compliance, “What is Communication Compliance?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In which Communication Compliance workflow stage might a reviewer mark an alert as a false positive or remove a Teams message?
notes.back: Remediate.
notes.explanation: Other options include tagging, notifying the user and escalating.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Communication Compliance, “What is Communication Compliance?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Communication Compliance workflow stage spans the whole process, using dashboard widgets, export logs and audit events?
notes.back: Maintain.
notes.explanation: It supports ongoing evaluation and improvement of compliance posture.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Communication Compliance, “What is Communication Compliance?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Can Communication Compliance check prompts and responses in generative AI apps?
notes.back: Yes: Microsoft 365 Copilot, apps built with Copilot Studio, and AI apps connected through supported connectors.
notes.explanation: This extends monitoring to AI conversations.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Communication Compliance, “Generative AI coverage”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which compliance area could a Communication Compliance policy serve by reviewing brokers’ messages for insider trading or bribery?
notes.back: Regulatory compliance.
notes.explanation: Corporate policies and risk management are the other listed areas.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Communication Compliance, “What is Communication Compliance?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Under which set of solutions in the Microsoft Purview portal is eDiscovery found?
notes.back: Risk & Compliance.
notes.explanation: All eDiscovery capabilities are in one interface, with premium features depending on licensing.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “Describe eDiscovery”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Microsoft 365 services can Purview eDiscovery search? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: Exchange Online, Microsoft Teams, Microsoft 365 Groups, OneDrive, SharePoint, Viva Engage.
notes.explanation: These are the supported services Microsoft lists.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “Describe eDiscovery”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does a user need before using any eDiscovery tool?
notes.back: The appropriate permissions assigned to them.
notes.explanation: Access to eDiscovery tools is not open to everyone.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “Describe eDiscovery”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What starts the eDiscovery workflow?
notes.back: A trigger event: an escalated activity that prompts a new case.
notes.explanation: Creating and managing the case is the next step.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: After searching and refining results in an eDiscovery case, which actions can you take? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: export the results, create review sets from them, create holds.
notes.explanation: Reviewing and acting within review sets comes after.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which actions can you take on items in a review set? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: run analytics to cull irrelevant data, tag items, export items, among others.
notes.explanation: Tags capture reviewers’ opinions on the content.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: In the eDiscovery workflow, what comes between escalating a trigger event and searching content?
notes.back: Creating and managing the case.
notes.explanation: The case then holds all the searches, holds and review sets.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When you add data to a review set, what happens to the original items?
notes.back: They stay in place; the items are copied into the review set.
notes.explanation: The review set gives a static, known set of content to work on.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery features and capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which premium eDiscovery feature extracts text from images added to a review set, so it can be searched?
notes.back: Optical character recognition.
notes.explanation: The image text is included with the content added to the review set.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery features and capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which premium eDiscovery feature lets you review a Teams chat message in the context of the whole back-and-forth?
notes.back: Conversation threading.
notes.explanation: It collects the entire thread when chat messages are added to a review set.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery features and capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What happens to documents protected by sensitivity labels when they are added to a premium review set?
notes.back: They are decrypted automatically.
notes.explanation: The same applies to email encrypted with Microsoft Purview Message Encryption.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery features and capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Are review sets a standard or a premium eDiscovery feature?
notes.back: Premium.
notes.explanation: Review sets can also predict relevance using predictive coding models.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery features and capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: When an insider risk case needs legal review, where can it be escalated?
notes.back: To a new case in eDiscovery.
notes.explanation: The integration helps risk and legal teams work together with a full view of the user’s activity.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “Integration with Microsoft Purview Insider Risk Management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Microsoft Entra ID activities does the unified audit log capture? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: user sign-ins, password changes, role assignments, Conditional Access policy changes.
notes.explanation: These are among many services whose activities it records.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “What the audit log captures”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Exchange Online activities does the unified audit log capture? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: message access, deletion, forwarding and replies; mailbox permission changes; user-created forwarding rules.
notes.explanation: Such records help show who did what, and when, during an investigation.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “What the audit log captures”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How are Microsoft 365 Copilot interactions recorded in the unified audit log?
notes.back: Automatically, as CopilotInteraction events, with no extra configuration.
notes.explanation: Each record notes the service used and any files accessed.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Microsoft 365 Copilot”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What must happen before Purview captures Microsoft Security Copilot interactions?
notes.back: A Copilot owner must opt in.
notes.explanation: Microsoft 365 Copilot is captured automatically, but Security Copilot needs this opt-in.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Copilot audit logging”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which audit data access method lets you search by activity, user and date range in the Microsoft Purview portal?
notes.back: The audit log search tool.
notes.explanation: Results can be exported for analysis in Excel.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Searching and accessing audit data”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which Exchange Online PowerShell cmdlet searches the unified audit log?
notes.back: Search-UnifiedAuditLog.
notes.explanation: It can be built into scripts for automated reporting.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Searching and accessing audit data”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Which audit access method lets you import audit records into a SIEM solution?
notes.back: The Office 365 Management Activity API.
notes.explanation: It gives programmatic access to audit records.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Searching and accessing audit data”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Does Audit Standard need to be switched on?
notes.back: No. It is enabled by default for organisations with the appropriate subscription.
notes.explanation: It is ready to use in most organisations without extra configuration.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Audit (Standard)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Audit Standard keeps audit records for {{c1::180}} days.
notes.explanation: That is enough to search roughly the past six months of activity.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Audit (Standard)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: After searching in Audit Standard, how can you analyse the results further?
notes.back: Export them to a comma-separated values file.
notes.explanation: Export is one of Audit Standard’s key capabilities.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Audit (Standard)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Under Audit Premium, which services’ audit records are kept for one year by default? Give two.
notes.back: Any two of: Microsoft Entra ID, Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint.
notes.explanation: Records of all other activities keep the 180-day default unless a retention policy says otherwise.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Audit (Premium)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: For how long can Audit Premium’s audit log retention policies keep records?
notes.back: Up to one year, or up to 10 years for users with the required add-on licence.
notes.explanation: Policies can target a service, specific activities or specific users.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Audit (Premium)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: What does Audit Premium’s higher bandwidth to the Office 365 Management Activity API allow?
notes.back: Pulling audit data faster.
notes.explanation: Microsoft notes this is especially valuable for large-scale investigations.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Audit (Premium)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How do intelligent insights help after a suspected breach?
notes.back: They help investigate possible breaches and determine the scope of an incident.
notes.explanation: They show events such as mail being accessed or forwarded.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Audit (Premium)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: An engineer who has resigned starts downloading large numbers of design files. Which Purview solution is built to detect and investigate this?
notes.back: C: Insider Risk Management.
notes.choices:
A) Communication Compliance
B) Audit Standard
C) Insider Risk Management
D) A retention label policy
notes.choicesExplained: A looks at messages, not file downloads. B records activity but does not detect risk or run cases. D sets how long content is kept.
notes.explanation: Data theft by departing users is a core Insider Risk Management scenario.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk management workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A reviewer decides an insider risk alert is harmless and dismisses it. Which workflow stage is this?
notes.back: A: triage.
notes.choices:
A) Triage
B) Investigate
C) Policies
D) Action
notes.choicesExplained: B happens inside a case after triage. C defines what is examined. D resolves cases, for example by escalating to eDiscovery.
notes.explanation: At triage reviewers open a case, add to one, or dismiss the alert.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe insider risk management in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk management workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A user has one low-severity insider risk alert and adaptive protection shows her a policy tip on sharing. Which risk level is she most likely at?
notes.back: B: Minor.
notes.choices:
A) Moderate
B) Minor
C) Elevated
D) Critical
notes.choicesExplained: A and C are for medium- and high-severity alerts and bring stronger controls. D is not one of the three insider risk levels.
notes.explanation: Low-severity alerts put a user at Minor, where light controls such as policy tips apply.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Insider risk levels”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A firm wants users flagged as high-risk by Insider Risk Management to lose access to its finance app automatically. Through which control would adaptive protection do this?
notes.back: C: Microsoft Entra Conditional Access.
notes.choices:
A) Data Lifecycle Management
B) Communication Compliance
C) Microsoft Entra Conditional Access
D) Audit Premium
notes.choicesExplained: A preserves deleted content. B reviews messages and is not an adaptive protection control. D records activity.
notes.explanation: Adaptive protection uses Conditional Access to restrict app access by insider risk level.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe adaptive protection in Microsoft Purview, “Adaptive protection in Conditional Access”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: The people team has had complaints of harassing language in Teams chats and wants such messages flagged for a reviewer. Which solution fits?
notes.back: B: Communication Compliance.
notes.choices:
A) Insider Risk Management
B) Communication Compliance
C) eDiscovery
D) Data loss prevention
notes.choicesExplained: A focuses on risky user activity such as data theft. C gathers evidence for legal cases. D stops sensitive data being shared, not abusive language.
notes.explanation: Communication Compliance checks messages for policy violations such as harassment.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Communication Compliance, “What is Communication Compliance?”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Lawyers fear a manager may delete emails relevant to a lawsuit. What should the eDiscovery team do first to protect them?
notes.back: B: place his mailbox on hold in the eDiscovery case.
notes.choices:
A) Export the mailbox to a laptop
B) Place his mailbox on hold in the eDiscovery case
C) Add a sensitivity label
D) Run analytics in a review set
notes.choicesExplained: A copies content but does not stop deletion at source. C protects access, not deletion. D culls data already collected.
notes.explanation: Holds preserve content from accidental or intentional deletion during an investigation.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery features and capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Reviewers need a fixed copy of collected items that they can tag and analyse without touching the originals. What should they use?
notes.back: B: a review set.
notes.choices:
A) A hold
B) A review set
C) Content explorer
D) The unified audit log
notes.choicesExplained: A preserves content in place but is not a workspace for tagging. C shows classified items but is not for legal review. D holds activity records, not collected content.
notes.explanation: A review set is a secure copy of collected items for search, filtering, tagging and analysis.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery features and capabilities”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A regulator demands all emails and Teams chats about a product recall as evidence. Which Purview solution is designed for this?
notes.back: B: eDiscovery.
notes.choices:
A) Compliance Manager
B) eDiscovery
C) Communication Compliance
D) Audit Standard
notes.choicesExplained: A tracks compliance with regulations. C flags inappropriate messages for review. D records who did what, not message content.
notes.explanation: eDiscovery identifies and delivers electronic information for use as evidence.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “Describe eDiscovery”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: An investigator on Audit Standard needs SharePoint file access records from ten months ago. What is the problem?
notes.back: A: Audit Standard keeps records for only 180 days.
notes.choices:
A) Audit Standard keeps records for only 180 days
B) SharePoint is not audited
C) Audit Standard must be switched on first
D) Only Global Administrators can search audit logs
notes.choicesExplained: B: SharePoint file access is captured. C: Audit Standard is on by default. D: users with the appropriate permissions can search.
notes.explanation: Audit Premium keeps SharePoint records for a year by default.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Audit (Standard)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: A regulated bank must keep audit records of certain users for seven years. What does it need?
notes.back: D: Audit Premium retention policies with the add-on licence.
notes.choices:
A) Audit Standard
B) Audit Premium with default settings
C) An eDiscovery hold
D) Audit Premium retention policies with the add-on licence
notes.choicesExplained: A keeps records for 180 days. B keeps some records for a year by default. C preserves content, not audit records.
notes.explanation: Without the add-on licence, audit log retention policies stop at one year, and the default periods are shorter still.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Audit (Premium)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: After a suspected breach, investigators want to know who changed a mailbox’s permissions last week. Where should they search?
notes.back: A: the unified audit log.
notes.choices:
A) The unified audit log
B) A review set
C) The file plan
D) Content explorer
notes.choicesExplained: B holds collected content, not activity records. C lists retention labels. D shows labelled or sensitive items, not permission changes.
notes.explanation: Mailbox permission changes are among the Exchange activities the log records.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “What the audit log captures”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: Under Audit Premium’s default settings, which of these records is kept for one year?
notes.back: A: a user’s OneDrive file download.
notes.choices:
A) A user’s OneDrive file download
B) A Teams meeting being changed
C) A Microsoft 365 admin centre configuration change
D) A Teams message being deleted
notes.choicesExplained: D, B and C come from services outside Entra ID, Exchange, OneDrive and SharePoint, so they keep the 180-day default.
notes.explanation: Audit Premium keeps Entra ID, Exchange, OneDrive and SharePoint records for a year by default.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Audit (Premium)”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does Insider Risk Management differ from Communication Compliance?
notes.back: Insider Risk Management looks at risky user behaviour across Microsoft 365; Communication Compliance looks at inappropriate messages.
notes.explanation: Both are insider risk solutions in Purview, and they integrate with each other.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe Communication Compliance, “Insider risk management”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does Audit Premium differ from Audit Standard?
notes.back: Premium adds longer retention, audit log retention policies, intelligent insights and more bandwidth for pulling audit data.
notes.explanation: Premium builds on all of Standard’s capabilities.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe audit in Microsoft Purview, “Two auditing solutions: Standard and Premium”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words

notes.front: How does an eDiscovery hold differ from a review set?
notes.back: A hold preserves content where it is; a review set copies collected items into a separate store for review.
notes.explanation: Both belong to an eDiscovery case.
notes.source: Microsoft Learn training: Describe eDiscovery, “eDiscovery workflow”
notes.sourceLicence: C · facts only, in our own words
